subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Show that z₁ = (2 + 11i)/25 and z₂ = (−2 + i)/(1 − 2i)² are conjugate to each other.

mark_split.label: Simplify z₂ to the form a + ib
Write the conjugate of z₂ and match it with z₁

recall_prompt: Say how you would show the two numbers are conjugates — what you simplify, how you divide, and what you compare at the end.
insider_note: z₁ is already finished, so all four marks sit on z₂: expand (1 − 2i)², divide by the conjugate, and only then compare. The denominator coming out as 25 — the same 25 as in z₁ — is the mid-question check that the arithmetic is right.

steps.label: Expand (1 − 2i)²
steps.margin_note: First mark. z₁ is already in the form a + ib, so all the work is on z₂. Start with its denominator: (1 − 2i)² = 1 − 4i + 4i² = −3 − 4i.
steps.memory_tip: (1 − 2i)² is an ordinary (p − q)²: 1 − 4i + 4i² = −3 − 4i. The middle term is not optional.

recall.must_convey: That the denominator (1 − 2i)² is expanded to −3 − 4i, so z₂ = (−2 + i)/(−3 − 4i), which is (2 − i)/(3 + 4i) after cancelling the minus.
accept: expand one minus two i squared to get minus three minus four i in the denominator
the denominator becomes minus three minus four i, then cancel the minus signs
one minus two i whole square is minus three minus four i
denominator lo one minus two i square cheste minus three minus four i vasthundi
square the denominator first using i squared equals minus one

steps.why: z₂ cannot be compared with z₁ until it is a single a + ib. The square in the denominator is the first thing standing in the way, and it is an ordinary (p − q)² with i² = −1.
common_mistakes: Writing (1 − 2i)² as 1 − 4i² = 5, forgetting the middle term.
Not cancelling the shared minus sign, which makes the next division messier.

steps.label: Simplify z₂
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Divide by multiplying top and bottom by the conjugate of the denominator, 3 − 4i. The bottom becomes 3² + 4² = 25 — the same 25 as in z₁, which is the first sign the answer is coming out right.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply top and bottom by 3 − 4i. The bottom becomes 3² + 4² = 25 — the same 25 as in z₁.

recall.must_convey: That z₂ is simplified by multiplying numerator and denominator by 3 − 4i, giving (2 − 11i)/25.
accept: multiply top and bottom by three minus four i and z two becomes two minus eleven i by twenty five
rationalise with the conjugate three minus four i, the denominator is twenty five and the numerator is two minus eleven i
z two simplifies to two minus eleven i over twenty five
conjugate three minus four i tho multiply cheste two minus eleven i by twenty five vasthundi
use the conjugate of the denominator to get two minus eleven i over twenty five

steps.why: Multiplying by the conjugate makes the denominator real, because (3 + 4i)(3 − 4i) = 3² + 4² has no i. That is the only standard way to write a complex quotient as a + ib.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by 3 + 4i instead of 3 − 4i, which leaves an i in the denominator.
Writing 4i² as +4 instead of −4 in the numerator.

steps.label: Compare with z₁
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The conjugate changes only the sign of the i term. Write the conjugate of z₂ and point at z₁.
steps.memory_tip: Conjugation flips only the i sign. Write the conjugate of z₂ and point at z₁ by name.

lines.text: ∴ z₁ and z₂ are conjugates of each other.

recall.must_convey: That the conjugate of (2 − 11i)/25 is (2 + 11i)/25, which is exactly z₁, so the two are conjugates.
accept: the conjugate of two minus eleven i by twenty five is two plus eleven i by twenty five which is z one
change the sign of the imaginary part of z two and you get z one
z two bar equals z one so they are conjugates
z two conjugate teeste z one vasthundi kabatti conjugates
flipping the sign of eleven i gives z one exactly

steps.why: Two numbers are conjugates when they have the same real part and opposite imaginary parts. Both have real part 2/25; the imaginary parts are −11/25 and +11/25. The sentence at the end is what earns the mark — the arithmetic alone is not an answer to 'show that'.
common_mistakes: Changing the sign of the real part as well.
Ending on (2 − 11i)/25 without writing its conjugate and naming z₁.
